t:
As used in and for the purposes of this title, unless the context indicates otherwise:

    (a) The word “cigarette” shall mean any roll of tobacco, or any substitute therefor, wrapped in paper or in any substance other than tobacco.
 
    (b) The word “person” shall mean any individual, partnership, corporation, association, receiver, executor, administrator, trustee, conservator, or other representative appointed by order of any court.
 
    (c) The word “District” shall mean the District of Columbia.
 
    (d) 
The word “Commissioners” shall mean the Commissioners of the District of Columbia.
 
    (e) 
The words “designated District agency” shall mean any officer, employee, department, office, or agency in or under the municipal government of the District of Columbia who or which is designated by the Commissioners to perform a function or duty under the terms and provisions of this Act.
 
    (f) 
The word “sell” or “sale” shall include offering for sale, keeping for sale, bartering, trafficking in, peddling, and any transfer or exchange in any manner or by any means for a consideration.
 
    (g) 
The term “original package” shall mean the individual package, parcel, or other container in which cigarettes are put up by the manufacturer to which is affixed the required United States Government Internal Revenue stamp, and the Commissioners may, by regulation, include within this definition any wrapper immediately enclosing such package, parcel, or other container.
 
    (h) 
The word “stamp” shall include impressions made by metering machines authorized to be used under the provisions of this title.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is only a definitions section with no outside-party process. However, subsection (g) authorizes the Commissioners to expand the definition of "original package" by regulation, and a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation even when it is discretionary ("may"). The label is uncertain because the Commissioners of the District of Columbia are arguably a municipal body rather than a federal agency.
fable.s: the Commissioners may, by regulation, include within this definition any wrapper immediately enclosing such package, parcel, or other container

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of definitions for terms used in the statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. While it mentions that Commissioners may make regulations, this is an internal administrative power and does not inherently require public participation or outside consultation in the text provided.
qwen_block.s: As used in and for the purposes of this title, unless the context indicates otherwise: (a) The word “cigarette” shall mean any roll of tobacco... (b) The word “person” shall mean any individual... (c) The word “District” shall mean the District of Columbia... (d) The word “Commissioners” shall mean the Commissioners of the District of Columbia... (e) The words “designated District agency” shall mean any officer, employee, department, office, or agency in or under the municipal government of the District of Columbia... (f) The word “sell” or “sale” shall include offering for sale... (g) The term “original package” shall mean the individual package... (h) The word “stamp” shall include impressions made by metering machines...

opus.w: Subsection (g) lets the Commissioners widen the definition of "original package" by regulation. Under the worked example, any authority to issue regulations counts as participation, even when it is optional, because rulemaking involves public input. The other subsections are plain definitions and would on their own be "No", but this grant of rulemaking power is enough for "Yes". This is less certain because the District of Columbia Commissioners are a municipal body rather than an ordinary federal agency.
opus.s: the Commissioners may, by regulation, include within this definition any wrapper immediately enclosing such package, parcel, or other container.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this is only a definitions section with nothing procedural in it. But subsection (g) lets the Commissioners act "by regulation." Under the rule in Example 6, a grant of regulatory authority counts as participation even when it is optional ("may"). There is a doubt here: the District of Columbia Commissioners are a municipal body, not a typical federal agency. Even so, the rulemaking rule seems to apply.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of definitions for terms used in the statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, comment, or participation by outside parties in a federal decision. The mention of regulations by the Commissioners refers to local DC government authority, not a federal participation mechanism.
qwen_chat.s: As used in and for the purposes of this title, unless the context indicates otherwise:
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions regulations by the Commissioners.
Resolution: The Commissioners are part of the local government of the District of Columbia, which is not the federal government in the context of this definition (or if considered federal, they are inside the government). More importantly, this section is purely definitional and does not establish a process for outside parties to participate in a federal decision.
